transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Aerolytix CTO), Samir Patel (Platform Eng), Lily Huang (NetOps), Evan Brooks (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick recap of last week's flake on the private pilot; focus on network egress shaping causing p95 spikes, and plan for kernel/driver upgrade + fallback routing hardening.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh Priya, Samir, Lily, thanks for making time. we're at week four of the private pilot so we wanted to run through the incidents, today's plan is: go over the egress shaping results, kernel upgrade plan, and the canary for latency.
[00:18] Priya: hi, yeah thanks, quick note, this is a slightly abbreviated crew today, Evan will join late. but yes, we saw the elevated p95 spikes last thursday around 03:12 UTC where some requests went from p50 ~42ms to p95 ~210ms.
[00:32] Diego: right, we pulled the traces, there's a clear tail originating from the netpath between your egress gateway and the internet; a combination of packet reordering and burst queueing. the app-level KV lookups themselves stayed consistent, so we think it's mostly network shaping.
[00:48] Samir: when you say "KV lookups", are you talking about the K-V cash? just making sure the movies are cached inter- — sorry the cache warmups are fine?
[00:57] Diego: yes, kv cache warmups looked good, the prefix cache had warm hits. the tail was after the kv layer, so we traced to the egress queueing. also noticed that our batcher occasionally gloms requests together during backlog and that changes serialization timing.
[01:15] Lily: so the netops angle: we confirmed MTU mismatch on two older edge boxes, and one of the eBPF packet-shapers has default queue length set low. we raised it to 512 and that reduced drop rate, but didn't fully remove spikes.
[01:30] Priya: curious, what's Redwood's fallback path behavior? we had a failover to the next region but it added 60ms which is unacceptable for some flows.
[01:38] Maya: good question — we have two fallbacks: a model-variant fallback (lower-LAT but cheaper model) and regional fallback. for this pilot we can set policy to prefer model-variant fallback over cross-region to keep latency bounded. but if the local GPU pool is saturated the model-variant fallback may increase cost.
[01:55] Evan (joins): sorry, late, got the calendar ping — can you catch me up on the kernel notes?
[02:03] Maya: sure. Diego, take the kernel upgrade?
[02:06] Diego: yes. we validated the newer NVIDIA driver + kernel combo on a small canary and saw reduced context switch stalls in our inference runtime. basically the kernel patch fixes a DMA scheduling edge that we saw in the flamegraphs. we recommend a rolling bump: 10% of nodes Thursday canary, then 30% if green.
[02:26] Evan: any risk to the KV cache persistence after a kernel bump?
[02:30] Diego: negligible; the runtime's KV checkpoint doesn't rely on kernel-specific shims, but the cold-start latency for large-context sessions might be ~15-20% longer immediately post-upgrade while the local caches rewarm.
[02:45] Samir: about telemetry — our SIEM needs audit logs forwarded with at least 30 day retention. do you provide raw audit events with SSO identity?
[02:55] Maya: we can forward audit logs; we support SAML and OIDC SSO mapping to principal names. retention for the hosted control plane is configurable as an add-on; for private we can either retain in the private control plane for 30/90/365 days or ship to your Kinesis/Splunk via the agent. I'll share the retention matrix.
[03:14] Lily: also, are the TLS origination points still at our edge or at Redwood's egress? last incident we saw a cert rotate and it tripped intermediate proxies.
[03:20] Maya: for Private the TLS termination remains in your VPC unless you opt into Redwood-managed certs. currently Aerolytix is terminating TLS at the egress, so cert rotation needs to be coordinated.
[03:32] Priya: ok, good. back to the egress shaping test — Diego, what's the recommended experiment to prove it's fixed?
[03:36] Diego: two things: run a synthetic high-concurrency burst test that mimics our production concurrency distribution (we'll provide the script), and run a 48h production-ish run while capturing p50/p90/p95 histograms plus packet-level traces for the top two endpoints. we'll correlate queue lengths and batch size changes.
[03:55] Maya: we'll share the script and can run it from Redwood if you give us a temporary token and an egress sandbox IP. also we'll attach the runbook for the canary kernel bump: https://redwood.example.com/pilot/aerolytix/runbook
[04:11] Samir: the token — we need it scoped to only the canary pool and TTL 4 hours; no write access to other infra.
[04:18] Maya: understood, we'll generate a scoped token.
[04:23] Evan: while we do the canary, what's the rollback plan if p95 regresses?
[04:26] Diego: rollback involves: (1) drain canary nodes, (2) switch traffic off the canary IPs, (3) restore previous kernel via image and rejoin. we have automation but we'll also prepare a manual runbook step in case the image rollback hits a driver loader issue.
[04:45] Lily: can we get a checklist? last time the rolling upgrade coincided with a cert rotation and that made it messy.
[04:50] Maya: yes, Diego will add cert/rotation checks to the checklist and Evan will validate monitoring alert thresholds pre-upgrade.
[04:58] Priya: another note: cost — last week we saw a burst double our token cost because the batcher compacted fewer requests and more tokens were served. any tuning knobs?
[05:08] Diego: batching config: you can cap batch size and reduce max latency window; Redwood Optimize has an auto-suggestion that will recommend quantization and batch limits based on throughput. we can apply a temporary cap to limit cost during canary.
[05:24] Priya: are there any compliance documents we should circulate? SOC2, encryption at rest with your KMS?
[05:29] Maya: yes, shared security pack already includes SOC2 type II report, KMS integration guide, and the private deployment hardening checklist. I'll resend the zip to the thread after the call.
[05:40] Samir: on fallback routing — can you explain the circuit breaker thresholds? we had one automatic fallback that flipped too early.
[05:46] Diego: circuit breaker is threshold-based (error rate and p95). current default is 5% errors OR p95 > 300ms sustained for 30s; for Aerolytix we suggest bumping the sustained window to 90s to avoid flapping. we can also require both conditions (error + latency) for higher tolerance.
[06:05] Lily: sounds good. also, can the fallback choose a lower-cost quantized model variant in the same region rather than cross-region?
[06:12] Maya: yes that's exactly the model-variant fallback we mentioned; we'll prefer that as default for your pilot. it's a config flag in your rollout policy.
[06:20] Priya: ok next steps then?
[06:22] Maya: recap: Redwood to share scripts + runbook + scoped token; Diego to collect p95 traces and prepare canary checklist; Aerolytix to confirm MTU and egress shaping screenshots and approve Thursday canary; Evan to validate monitoring alerts and rollback playbook. We'll reconvene after the 48h run and the canary — propose Monday follow-up if results are green.
[06:45] Priya: monday follow-up works. thanks everyone.
[06:50] Maya: thanks — we'll follow up with links and action items.
